problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence grants a finding that supports the old assumption: many birds rejected the caterpillars after tasting them, which fits the idea of learned distaste. The next sentence adds a finding that this explanation can't fully account for: birds with no experience avoided the caterpillars on sight alone. That pattern of conceding a point and then turning against it calls for D, "Even so." A is wrong because it suggests the tasting results caused the naive birds to avoid the caterpillars, but these were two different groups of birds. B is wrong because "Instead" implies the first finding is being replaced, yet the tasting results still stand. C is wrong because "In other words" introduces a restatement, while the second sentence presents a new, contrasting result.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장의 "many birds did reject"(양보 신호)와 뒤 문장의 "rather than learned distaste alone"(기존 설명의 한계)을 연결해야 D(Even so)가 확정됨. A는 훑어 읽으면 인과로 오인 가능, B는 대비 방향은 맞으나 앞 사실을 대체하는 의미라 배제, C는 재진술이 아니므로 배제. 두 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 배경 지식(진홍나방 애벌레의 금방망이 알칼로이드 저장)도 사실과 부합하며, 연구자·실험은 가상으로 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 앞 문장은 기존 가정을 뒷받침하는 결과를 인정하고, 뒤 문장은 그 가정만으로는 설명되지 않는 결과를 제시하므로 양보 후 반전의 Even so가 성립한다. Instead는 대조 신호어라 훑어 읽으면 고를 수 있지만, 앞의 결과가 여전히 유효하므로 대체 관계는 성립하지 않는다. As a result도 앞뒤 결과를 섣불리 연결하면 그럴듯해 보인다. medium 수준에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Mechanics' institutes were founded in Britain beginning in the 1820s to offer evening instruction to working people.
- The London Mechanics' Institute opened in 1823; by 1850, roughly 700 such institutes existed across Britain.
- Mechanics' institutes concentrated mainly on science and technical subjects useful in trades.
- The first working men's college opened in London in 1854.
- Working men's colleges offered history, literature, and drawing alongside practical subjects.

The student wants to contrast the subjects taught at the two types of institutions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Mechanics' institutes were founded in Britain beginning in the 1820s to offer evening instruction to working people.
- The London Mechanics' Institute opened in 1823; by 1850, roughly 700 such institutes existed across Britain.
- Mechanics' institutes concentrated mainly on science and technical subjects useful in trades.

problem.question: The student wants to contrast the subjects taught at the two types of institutions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Mechanics' institutes, which began in the 1820s, were followed in 1854 by the first working men's college, which opened in London.
By 1850, roughly 700 mechanics' institutes, focused mainly on science and technical trade subjects, were operating across Britain.
Whereas mechanics' institutes concentrated mainly on science and technical trade subjects, working men's colleges also taught history, literature, and drawing.
Both mechanics' institutes and working men's colleges offered instruction to working people in Britain, with London hosting early examples of each.
problem.explanation: 목표는 두 기관의 교과 내용을 대조하는 것이다. C는 기계공 강습소의 과학·기술 중심 교육과 노동자 대학의 역사·문학·미술 교육을 'Whereas'로 직접 대조하므로 정답이다. A는 두 기관을 언급하지만 교과가 아니라 설립 시기만 비교한다. B는 교과를 언급하지만 한 기관에 대해서만 말하므로 대조가 없다. D는 차이가 아니라 공통점을 강조한다.
problem.explanationEn: The goal is to contrast what was taught at the two types of institutions. C is correct because it uses "Whereas" to set the institutes' focus on science and technical subjects directly against the colleges' broader offerings of history, literature, and drawing. A mentions both institutions, but it compares when they were founded, not what they taught. B does mention subjects, but it covers only the mechanics' institutes, so there is no contrast. D points out what the two institutions had in common rather than how they differed.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 'Whereas'로 두 기관의 교과를 직접 대조하며 노트 내용(과학·기술 vs 역사·문학·드로잉)과 일치. A는 두 기관 모두 언급하나 시기 비교, B는 교과 언급하나 한 기관만, D는 공통점 강조로 각각 부분적 근거가 있어 비교 배제가 필요함. 역사 사실(1823 런던 기계공 강습소, 1854 노동자 대학, ~700개)도 통설과 부합. 해설 한·영 모두 정답과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 'also taught'가 'alongside practical subjects' 의미를 담아 노트 정보 충실.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 노트 3·5를 정확히 대조함('also'는 노트 5의 alongside practical subjects와 일치). 오답 A(두 기관이지만 시기), B(교과지만 한 기관), D(두 기관이지만 공통점)가 각각 부분 근거를 지녀 medium에 적합. 다만 'Whereas' 신호어로 정답이 다소 쉽게 드러날 수 있음.

problem.passage:
When railroads in the United States and Canada adopted standard time zones in 1883, many observers treated the change as a narrow technical fix for confusing train timetables, and railway officials stressed exactly that purpose in their public announcements. ______ the new zones soon reshaped daily routines far beyond the stations: in many towns, factories, schools, and churches reset their clocks to "railroad time," sometimes over the objections of residents who preferred to keep noon set by the sun.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When railroads in the United States and Canada adopted standard time zones in 1883, many observers treated the change as a narrow technical fix for confusing train timetables, and railway officials stressed exactly that purpose in their public announcements. ______ the new zones soon reshaped daily routines far beyond the stations: in many towns, factories, schools, and churches reset their clocks to "railroad time," sometimes over the objections of residents who preferred to keep noon set by the sun.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 첫 문장은 표준시 도입이 열차 시간표만을 위한 좁은 기술적 조치로 여겨졌고 철도 관계자들도 그 목적을 강조했다는 점을 인정한다. 다음 문장은 실제로는 역 바깥의 일상생활까지 바꾸었다고 하므로, 앞의 인식과 반대되는 사실을 제시하는 양보 후 반전 관계이며 D가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장에 공장·학교 같은 구체적 사례가 나오지만, 이 문장은 '좁은 기술적 조치'라는 앞의 주장을 예시하는 게 아니라 반박한다. B는 공식 발표가 기술적 목적을 강조한 것이 일상생활 변화의 원인은 아니므로 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. C는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용을 덧붙이는 게 아니라 대조를 이루므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence grants that people saw standard time as a narrow technical fix for train timetables, and that officials stressed exactly that purpose. The second sentence says the zones actually changed daily life far beyond the railroads. That contradicts the narrow view, so this is a concession followed by a reversal, and D is correct. A is tempting because the second sentence lists specific examples (factories, schools), but those examples argue against the first sentence's claim instead of illustrating it. B doesn't work because officials stressing a technical purpose didn't cause towns to reset their clocks, so the cause-and-effect link is wrong. C is wrong because the second sentence contrasts with the first; it doesn't add a similar point.

hardJudge.note: 첫 문장(좁은 기술적 조치로 인식·공식 강조)과 둘째 문장(실제로는 일상 전반을 재편)의 양보-반전 관계가 명확하여 'Even so'가 유일하게 성립. B는 '도입→변화'로 훑어 읽으면 인과로 오인할 수 있고, A는 뒤 문장의 구체 사례 때문에 매력적이어서 비교 판단이 필요함. 1883년 북미 철도 표준시 도입과 '철도 시간' 채택을 둘러싼 지역 반발은 역사적 사실과 부합. 한·영 해설 결론과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: 1883년 미국·캐나다 철도의 표준시 도입과 지역 사회의 '철도 시간' 채택은 사실이다. 양보 후 반전 구조이므로 정답 D(Even so)가 맞다. A는 뒤 문장에 공장·학교 같은 구체적 사례가 나와서 고르기 쉽고, B는 철도 관계자의 발표 때문에 일상이 바뀌었다고 잘못 연결하게 만드는 함정이라 둘 다 오답으로서 그럴듯하다. 훑어 읽으면 틀리기 쉬운 문항이어서 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The bombardier beetle (Brachinus crepitans) defends itself by spraying a hot chemical mixture at predators.
- The beetle stores two chemicals, hydroquinones and hydrogen peroxide, in a reservoir inside its abdomen.
- When threatened, it pushes these chemicals into a separate reaction chamber lined with enzymes.
- The enzymes trigger a rapid reaction that heats the mixture to about 100°C (212°F).
- The beetle releases the spray in rapid pulses of roughly 500 per second rather than as a continuous stream.
- Researchers believe the pulsing allows fresh liquid to cool the chamber between bursts, protecting the beetle's own tissues from heat damage.

The student wants to explain how the bombardier beetle avoids being harmed by its own defensive spray. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The bombardier beetle (Brachinus crepitans) defends itself by spraying a hot chemical mixture at predators.
- The beetle stores two chemicals, hydroquinones and hydrogen peroxide, in a reservoir inside its abdomen.
- When threatened, it pushes these chemicals into a separate reaction chamber lined with enzymes.
- The enzymes trigger a rapid reaction that heats the mixture to about 100°C (212°F).
- The beetle releases the spray in rapid pulses of roughly 500 per second rather than as a continuous stream.
- Researchers believe the pulsing allows fresh liquid to cool the chamber between bursts, protecting the beetle's own tissues from heat damage.
problem.question: The student wants to explain how the bombardier beetle avoids being harmed by its own defensive spray. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although its spray reaches about 100°C, the bombardier beetle releases it in rapid pulses, which likely let fresh liquid cool the reaction chamber and keep the beetle's tissues from being damaged.
The bombardier beetle keeps hydroquinones and hydrogen peroxide in an abdominal reservoir and pushes them into a separate enzyme-lined chamber only when it is threatened.
When threatened by a predator, the bombardier beetle produces a chemical spray that enzymes heat to about 100°C, making it an effective defense.
The bombardier beetle releases its hot defensive spray in rapid pulses of roughly 500 per second rather than as a continuous stream.
problem.explanation: 목표는 딱정벌레가 자신의 분사액에 어떻게 해를 입지 않는지 설명하는 것이므로, 고온이라는 위험과 박동식 분사가 반응실을 식혀 조직을 보호한다는 메커니즘을 연결해야 한다. A는 이 두 정보를 결합해 목표를 달성한다. B는 화학물질을 분리 저장한다는 사실만 전할 뿐, 그것이 자기 보호와 어떻게 이어지는지는 설명하지 않는다. C는 분사액이 포식자에게 효과적인 방어 수단이라는 점에 초점을 맞추어 자기 보호라는 목표에서 벗어난다. D는 박동식 분사를 언급하지만 그것이 냉각과 조직 보호로 이어진다는 핵심 연결이 빠져 있다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain how the beetle keeps from being harmed by its own spray, so the answer needs to connect the danger (a spray at about 100°C) with the protective mechanism (pulses that let fresh liquid cool the chamber). Choice A makes that connection and accomplishes the goal. Choice B describes how the chemicals are stored separately but never explains how that protects the beetle. Choice C focuses on how well the spray works against predators, which is not the same as self-protection. Choice D mentions the pulses but leaves out the key link to cooling and tissue protection.

hardJudge.note: A는 100°C 고온(위험)과 500회/초 박동식 분사→냉각→조직 보호(메커니즘)를 결합해 목표를 정확히 달성하며, 'likely'는 노트의 'Researchers believe'와 부합. D는 박동식 분사만 언급(핵심 연결 누락), B는 분리 저장(자기 보호로 오해 가능하나 노트에 근거 없음)으로 비교가 필요한 부분 정답형 오답이고, C는 방어 효과에 초점으로 목표 이탈. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 폭탄먼지벌레 관련 사실 정확.

advisory.note: D는 박동을 언급하지만 냉각과의 연결이 빠진 그럴듯한 오답이고, B는 분리 저장이 보호와 관련 있는 것처럼 보이는 함정이라 medium 난이도에 적합하다. A만 유일하게 목표를 충족한다.

problem.passage:
When engineers in the Netherlands began testing roads paved with recycled plastic modules in 2018, critics predicted the hollow sections would crack under the weight of delivery trucks. Early load trials seemed to support this worry: several prototype panels deformed after only a few weeks of heavy traffic. ______ redesigned panels reinforced with internal ribbing have since carried bus traffic for over two years without measurable warping, and they drain rainwater faster than conventional asphalt does.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When engineers in the Netherlands began testing roads paved with recycled plastic modules in 2018, critics predicted the hollow sections would crack under the weight of delivery trucks. Early load trials seemed to support this worry: several prototype panels deformed after only a few weeks of heavy traffic. ______ redesigned panels reinforced with internal ribbing have since carried bus traffic for over two years without measurable warping, and they drain rainwater faster than conventional asphalt does.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 초기 시험이 비판자들의 우려를 뒷받침하는 듯했다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 재설계된 패널이 오랫동안 변형 없이 버텼다는 반대 방향의 결과를 제시한다. 따라서 앞 내용을 인정한 뒤 반전하는 B가 가장 논리적이다. A는 개선된 패널이 초기 실패의 결과처럼 보일 수 있지만, 뒤 문장은 실패가 낳은 결과가 아니라 우려와 대조되는 성과를 강조하므로 맞지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장과 비슷한 사례로 다루지만 두 문장의 내용은 서로 반대다. D는 뒤 문장을 패널 변형의 구체적 사례로 보지만, 뒤 문장은 변형이 일어나지 않은 경우를 다룬다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence says early trials seemed to support the critics' worry, while the next sentence reports the opposite outcome: redesigned panels lasted for years without warping. So you need a transition that accepts the earlier point and then reverses it, which is what B does. A might seem to work because the redesign came after the failures, but the sentence is not presented as a result of those failures; it stresses success in contrast to the worry. C treats the two sentences as similar, but they actually point in opposite directions. D would introduce an example of panels deforming, but the sentence describes panels that did not deform.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(초기 시험이 우려를 뒷받침하는 듯함)과 뒤 문장(재설계 패널의 장기 성공)이 대조 관계이므로 양보·반전 전환어 B가 정답. A는 시간적 선후 때문에 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이며, C·D는 논리 방향이 맞지 않음. 해설(한·영) 일치하고 글자 참조 정확. 네덜란드 플라스틱 도로(PlasticRoad) 소재는 실제 사례와 유사하나 구체 수치는 허구적 서술로 저작권 문제 없음. 난이도는 'seemed to support'라는 단서와 두 문장 비교가 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 우려를 뒷받침하는 초기 실패 다음에 재설계 패널의 성공이 이어지므로 양보·대조 관계이고, 정답 'Even so'가 옳다. 'Consequently'는 재설계가 실패 뒤에 나왔다는 점 때문에 그럴듯한 오답이다. C와 D는 비교적 약한 오답이지만 중간 난이도에 대체로 적합하다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Engineers often protect buildings in earthquake zones with base isolation, which places flexible bearings between a building and its foundation.
- In 2019, engineers in Chile retrofitted a 1920s hospital in Valparaíso by installing 84 rubber-and-lead bearings beneath it.
- The bearings allow the ground to shift while the building above moves far less.
- Another approach, tuned mass damping, uses a heavy weight near the top of a tall building that sways opposite to the structure's motion.
- Taipei 101 in Taiwan uses a 660-metric-ton steel sphere suspended between its 87th and 92nd floors as a tuned mass damper.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in where the two earthquake-protection approaches place their key components. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Engineers often protect buildings in earthquake zones with base isolation, which places flexible bearings between a building and its foundation.
- In 2019, engineers in Chile retrofitted a 1920s hospital in Valparaíso by installing 84 rubber-and-lead bearings beneath it.
- The bearings allow the ground to shift while the building above moves far less.
- Another approach, tuned mass damping, uses a heavy weight near the top of a tall building that sways opposite to the structure's motion.
- Taipei 101 in Taiwan uses a 660-metric-ton steel sphere suspended between its 87th and 92nd floors as a tuned mass damper.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference in where the two earthquake-protection approaches place their key components. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Both base isolation and tuned mass damping are used to protect buildings, as shown by a hospital in Valparaíso, Chile, and by Taipei 101 in Taiwan.
Taipei 101's tuned mass damper, a 660-metric-ton steel sphere, sways opposite to the building's motion, while the Valparaíso hospital's bearings let the ground shift beneath it.
In 2019, engineers retrofitted a 1920s hospital in Valparaíso, Chile, with 84 rubber-and-lead bearings, an example of base isolation.
Whereas base isolation places flexible bearings between a building and its foundation, tuned mass damping relies on a heavy weight positioned near the top of a tall building.
problem.explanation: 목표는 두 방식이 핵심 부품을 '어디에' 두는지의 차이를 강조하는 것이다. D는 base isolation은 건물과 기초 사이, tuned mass damping은 건물 상부라는 위치를 대조하므로 정답이다. A는 두 방식의 공통점(건물 보호)만 말할 뿐 위치 차이를 제시하지 않는다. B는 두 방식을 대조하지만 차이를 위치가 아닌 작동 방식(반대로 흔들림, 지면 이동)으로 설명한다. C는 한 가지 방식만 다루어 비교가 이루어지지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to highlight a difference in where each approach puts its key components. D does this: it says base isolation puts bearings between a building and its foundation, while tuned mass damping puts a weight near the top of the building. A points out only what the two approaches have in common, which is that both protect buildings, and says nothing about location. B does contrast the approaches, but it compares how they work (swaying in the opposite direction vs. letting the ground shift), not where their parts are placed. C describes only one approach, so there is no comparison at all.

hardJudge.note: D는 두 방식의 핵심 부품 위치(건물-기초 사이 vs. 건물 상부)를 명시적으로 대조하므로 정답이 맞다. B는 두 방식을 대조하고 'beneath it'으로 위치를 부분적으로 암시하여 그럴듯한 오답이며, A는 공통점만, C는 한 방식만 제시해 배제된다. 해설(한·영) 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. Taipei 101 댐퍼 수치(660톤, 87~92층)는 사실과 부합. 정답 문장이 노트 문구를 거의 그대로 결합해 다소 직접적이지만, 목표(위치 차이)와 B의 작동 방식 대조를 구별해야 하므로 medium에 부합한다.

advisory.note: Taipei 101 정보(660톤, 87~92층)는 사실과 맞음. Valparaíso 병원 개보수 사례는 검증하기 어렵지만 학생 노트 형식이므로 허용 가능. B는 대조 구조이고 'beneath'라는 단어가 있어 그럴듯한 오답으로 작동함. D만 두 방식의 위치를 직접 대조함.

problem.passage:
Ecologists long assumed that the bright orange coloration of the Pacific newt's belly served mainly to warn predators of the toxin in its skin. When biologist Lena Ortiz tested this idea, she found that garter snakes from populations that had evolved resistance to the toxin attacked brightly colored and dull-painted model newts at nearly identical rates. ______ the coloration may not deter the very predators most likely to encounter newts, prompting Ortiz to propose that the orange belly may instead play a role in mate recognition.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Ecologists long assumed that the bright orange coloration of the Pacific newt's belly served mainly to warn predators of the toxin in its skin. When biologist Lena Ortiz tested this idea, she found that garter snakes from populations that had evolved resistance to the toxin attacked brightly colored and dull-painted model newts at nearly identical rates. ______ the coloration may not deter the very predators most likely to encounter newts, prompting Ortiz to propose that the orange belly may instead play a role in mate recognition.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 실험 결과(내성 있는 뱀이 밝은 모형과 칙칙한 모형을 거의 같은 비율로 공격함)를 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과에서 끌어낸 결론(색이 주요 포식자를 막지 못할 수 있음)을 말하므로 결과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 지문 전체가 기존 가정과 대조되기 때문에 그럴듯해 보이지만, 빈칸 앞뒤 문장은 서로 반대되지 않고 같은 방향으로 이어진다. B는 뒤 문장이 구체적 사례처럼 보일 수 있으나, 실제로는 실험 결과에서 나온 일반적 결론이므로 맞지 않는다. D는 두 문장이 평행한 별개의 사실이 아니라 근거와 결론의 관계이므로 부적절하다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives an experimental result: toxin-resistant snakes attacked bright and dull model newts at nearly the same rate. The sentence after the blank draws a conclusion from that result, namely that the coloration may not deter key predators, so C, a transition showing consequence, is correct. A may seem tempting because the passage as a whole challenges an older assumption, but the two sentences around the blank point in the same direction rather than contradicting each other. B fails because the second sentence is not a specific example of the first; it is a broader conclusion drawn from it. D is wrong because the sentences are not two parallel, similar facts; one is evidence and the other is the inference based on it.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 실험 결과(밝은/칙칙한 모형 공격률 동일) → 빈칸 뒤 결론(색이 포식자 억제 안 함)의 인과 관계이므로 C 'Thus'가 정답임을 직접 확인. A는 지문 전체의 대조 구조 때문에 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하여 medium 난이도에 적합. 해설 한/영 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 가상의 연구자/연구로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 결과에서 결론으로 이어지는 관계가 분명하므로 'Thus'가 정답이다. A는 지문 전체가 기존 가정과 대조된다는 점 때문에 그럴듯한 오답이 된다. B와 D는 다소 약하지만 말은 되므로 medium 난이도로 볼 수 있다. 연구자 Lena Ortiz는 가상 인물로 보인다. 다만 내성이 있는 뱀이 독이 있다는 경고를 무시한다는 사실은 결론과 자연스럽게 연결된다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Novelist Margarethe Ilsley published The Lantern House in 2016.
- The novel imitates the style of nineteenth-century Gothic fiction, with long sentences, a decaying manor, and letters exchanged between characters.
- Ilsley's earlier novel, Salt Roads (2009), was set in a contemporary city and written in short, plain sentences.
- The Lantern House is narrated by a housekeeper who never reveals her name.
- Salt Roads is narrated by a taxi driver who addresses readers directly by name in every chapter.

The student wants to contrast the narrators of the two novels. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Novelist Margarethe Ilsley published The Lantern House in 2016.
- The novel imitates the style of nineteenth-century Gothic fiction, with long sentences, a decaying manor, and letters exchanged between characters.
- Ilsley's earlier novel, Salt Roads (2009), was set in a contemporary city and written in short, plain sentences.
- The Lantern House is narrated by a housekeeper who never reveals her name.
- Salt Roads is narrated by a taxi driver who addresses readers directly by name in every chapter.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast the narrators of the two novels. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Unlike Salt Roads (2009), which uses short, plain sentences, Ilsley's The Lantern House (2016) imitates nineteenth-century Gothic fiction with long sentences and a decaying manor.
The Lantern House is narrated by a housekeeper who never reveals her name, whereas the taxi driver who narrates Salt Roads addresses readers directly by name in every chapter.
Both of Ilsley's novels use a single narrator: a housekeeper in The Lantern House and a taxi driver in Salt Roads.
Narrated by a nameless housekeeper, The Lantern House (2016) features letters exchanged between characters in the manner of nineteenth-century Gothic fiction.
problem.explanation: 목표는 두 소설의 '화자'를 대조하는 것이다. B는 이름을 밝히지 않는 가정부 화자와 매 장 독자를 이름으로 직접 부르는 택시 기사 화자를 whereas로 대조하므로 정답이다. A는 두 소설을 대조하지만 화자가 아니라 문체·배경을 대조한다. C는 두 화자를 언급하지만 '공통점'을 강조하며 대조가 되지 않는다. D는 한 소설만 다루므로 대조가 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to contrast the two novels' narrators. B does this: it sets the housekeeper who never reveals her name against the taxi driver who addresses readers by name, linked by "whereas." A does contrast the two novels, but it compares style and setting, not narrators. C names both narrators but stresses what they share, so it isn't a contrast. D covers only The Lantern House, so there's nothing to contrast it with.

hardJudge.note: B만이 두 소설의 화자(이름을 밝히지 않는 가정부 vs 독자를 이름으로 부르는 택시 기사)를 'whereas'로 직접 대조하며 노트 내용과 일치. A는 대조 구조이나 문체·배경 대조(화자 아님), C는 두 화자를 언급하나 공통점 강조, D는 단일 소설만 다룸 — 오답 중 A·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교 판단이 필요하므로 medium 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음, 가상의 작가·작품으로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: B의 대조축이 약간 비대칭이다(화자 자신의 이름을 숨김 vs 독자의 이름을 부름). 그래도 두 화자를 대조하므로 정답으로 인정된다. C의 'single narrator'는 메모에 명시되지 않은 내용이지만 오답이므로 문제없다. 오답 A·C·D가 각각 부분 근거(대조 구조, 두 화자 언급, 화자 언급)를 갖고 있어 medium 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
In the early nineteenth century, many British towns relied on local "time" set by the position of the sun, so clocks in Bristol ran about ten minutes behind those in London. Railway companies, which needed coordinated timetables, began adopting London time for their schedules in the 1840s. Some town councils initially resisted, insisting that local noon was the only natural standard. ______ by the mid-1850s most public clocks in Britain displayed railway time, often with a second minute hand added so that residents could still consult the old local time if they wished.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In the early nineteenth century, many British towns relied on local "time" set by the position of the sun, so clocks in Bristol ran about ten minutes behind those in London. Railway companies, which needed coordinated timetables, began adopting London time for their schedules in the 1840s. Some town councils initially resisted, insisting that local noon was the only natural standard. ______ by the mid-1850s most public clocks in Britain displayed railway time, often with a second minute hand added so that residents could still consult the old local time if they wished.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 일부 시의회가 철도 시간에 저항했다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그런데도 1850년대 중반에는 대부분의 공공 시계가 철도 시간을 표시했다고 말한다. 저항이 있었는데도 결국 채택되었으므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 철도 회사의 채택이 확산을 불러온 원인처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 바로 앞 문장은 '저항'이라서 확산의 원인이 될 수 없다. C는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장(저항)의 사례로 만드는데, 뒤 문장은 오히려 저항과 반대되는 결과다. D는 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 두 문장은 비슷하지 않고 서로 대조된다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank says some town councils resisted railway time, and the sentence after says that by the mid-1850s most public clocks showed railway time anyway. Railway time was adopted even though there was resistance, so the transition has to show a concession followed by a contrast, and that makes A correct. B is tempting because the railways' choice did help spread railway time, but the sentence right before the blank is about resistance, and resistance can't be the cause of the spread. C would make the second sentence an example of the resistance, but that sentence describes the opposite outcome. D signals that a similar idea is being added, but these two sentences contrast with each other instead.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(시의회의 저항)과 뒤 문장(그럼에도 대부분 철도 시간 채택)이 명확히 대조되어 A 'Nevertheless'가 정답. B 'Consequently'는 두 문장 앞의 철도 회사 채택을 원인으로 오독하면 끌리는 강한 오답이며, D는 앞선 철도 회사 채택 내용과의 유사성으로 약간의 근거가 있음. C는 가장 약하나 말이 됨. 역사적 사실(브리스틀 약 10분 차, 1840년대 철도 시간 도입, 1850년대 중반 대부분 공공 시계 GMT 표시, 이중 분침)은 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 같은 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어에 한글 없음. 난이도는 표준 SAT medium에 부합.

advisory.note: 정답 A(Nevertheless)가 맞다. 빈칸 앞 문장은 시의회의 저항이고, 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 철도 시간이 퍼졌다는 내용이라 양보 후 반전 관계다. B(Consequently)는 앞의 앞 문장(철도 회사의 채택)과 연결하면 그럴듯해서, 바로 앞 문장까지 정독해야 배제된다. 따라서 medium 난이도에 맞다. 역사적 사실도 대체로 정확하다. 브리스틀은 약 10분 차이였고, 1840년대에 철도가 런던 시간을 채택했으며, 1855년 무렵 대부분의 공공 시계가 철도 시간을 표시했다. 다만 분침이 두 개인 시계는 브리스틀 콘 익스체인지 시계 같은 사례가 있지만, 'often'은 다소 과장일 수 있다(경미한 사항).

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the nineteenth century, many European cities began installing public street lighting.
- London adopted gas streetlamps on a large scale beginning in the 1810s; the lamps had to be lit by hand each evening by workers called lamplighters.
- Paris, by contrast, introduced electric arc lamps along the Avenue de l'Opéra in 1878.
- Electric arc lamps needed no nightly hand lighting and gave off a far brighter light than gas lamps.
- Historians note that brighter, more reliable street lighting encouraged shops, cafés, and theaters to stay open later.

The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two lighting technologies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the nineteenth century, many European cities began installing public street lighting.
- London adopted gas streetlamps on a large scale beginning in the 1810s; the lamps had to be lit by hand each evening by workers called lamplighters.
- Paris, by contrast, introduced electric arc lamps along the Avenue de l'Opéra in 1878.
- Electric arc lamps needed no nightly hand lighting and gave off a far brighter light than gas lamps.
- Historians note that brighter, more reliable street lighting encouraged shops, cafés, and theaters to stay open later.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two lighting technologies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: London adopted gas streetlamps beginning in the 1810s, while Paris introduced electric arc lamps along the Avenue de l'Opéra in 1878.
Both London's gas lamps and Paris's electric arc lamps were part of a nineteenth-century movement to install public street lighting in European cities.
Brighter, more reliable street lighting, such as the electric arc lamps introduced in Paris in 1878, encouraged shops, cafés, and theaters to stay open later.
Whereas gas streetlamps had to be lit by hand each evening by lamplighters, electric arc lamps required no nightly hand lighting and shone far more brightly.
problem.explanation: 목표는 두 조명 기술 자체의 차이를 강조하는 것이다. D는 가스등은 매일 저녁 손으로 켜야 했지만 전기 아크등은 그럴 필요가 없고 훨씬 밝았다는 점을 대조해 기술 간 차이를 직접 보여준다. A는 대조 형식을 갖추었지만 기술의 차이가 아니라 도입 도시와 시기의 차이만 말한다. B는 차이가 아니라 두 기술의 공통점을 강조한다. C는 밝은 조명이 상업에 미친 영향을 설명할 뿐 두 기술을 비교하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to emphasize a difference between the two lighting technologies themselves. D does this directly: it contrasts gas lamps, which had to be lit by hand every evening, with electric arc lamps, which needed no hand lighting and were much brighter. A is set up as a contrast, but it contrasts the cities and dates of adoption, not how the technologies work. B points out what the two have in common rather than how they differ. C describes how bright lighting affected businesses, but it never compares the two technologies.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산 완료: 노트 2·4의 내용을 결합해 두 기술의 작동상 차이(수동 점등 vs 불필요, 밝기)를 직접 대조함. A는 대조 구조를 갖추었으나 도시·시기 차이만 제시해 유력한 오답 역할을 하고, C는 노트 정보를 정확히 쓰되 비교가 없으며, B는 공통점 서술로 말이 되는 오답. 두 단계 판단(과제 식별 + '기술의 차이'와 '도시의 차이' 구분)을 요구하므로 medium 적합. 사실 관계(런던 1810년대 가스등, 파리 1878년 오페라 거리 아크등) 역사적으로 타당. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: A는 대조 구조를 갖추고 있어 매력적인 오답이다. C는 아크등을 언급하지만 비교하지 않는다. 표준 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
When the first public lending libraries opened in English mill towns in the 1850s, reformers predicted that factory workers would use them mainly to borrow technical manuals and improve their trade skills. Circulation records from the Manchester Free Library, however, tell a different story: novels, travel narratives, and serialized adventure stories made up the large majority of loans to working-class patrons. ______ historians now argue that these libraries did less to reshape workers' labor than to give them access to leisure reading that had previously been affordable only to the middle classes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When the first public lending libraries opened in English mill towns in the 1850s, reformers predicted that factory workers would use them mainly to borrow technical manuals and improve their trade skills. Circulation records from the Manchester Free Library, however, tell a different story: novels, travel narratives, and serialized adventure stories made up the large majority of loans to working-class patrons. ______ historians now argue that these libraries did less to reshape workers' labor than to give them access to leisure reading that had previously been affordable only to the middle classes.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 대출 기록이 주로 소설·여행기 등 여가 독서였다는 증거를 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 증거에 근거해 역사가들이 도서관의 역할을 여가 독서 확대로 해석한다는 결론을 내린다. 따라서 근거에서 결론으로 이어지는 C가 정답이다. A는 개혁가들의 예측과 실제 기록 사이의 대조에 이끌린 오답인데, 그 반전은 이미 'however'로 처리되었고 뒤 문장은 기록과 일치하므로 양보 관계가 아니다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 구체적 사례가 아니라 해석·결론이므로 틀리다. D 역시 앞뒤 문장이 서로 대조되지 않고 같은 방향을 가리키므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives evidence: loan records show working-class patrons mostly borrowed novels and other leisure reading. The sentence after it draws a conclusion from that evidence: historians see the libraries mainly as a way to open up leisure reading. Because the text moves from evidence to conclusion, C is correct. A plays on the gap between the reformers' prediction and the actual records, but "however" already marks that reversal, and the final sentence agrees with the records instead of conceding a point. B is wrong because the last sentence interprets the evidence rather than giving an example of it. D is wrong because the two sentences point in the same direction and don't contrast.

hardJudge.note: 지문 흐름(예측 → however 기록 → 빈칸 → 역사가 결론)에서 증거→결론 관계이므로 'Accordingly'가 유일하게 성립. A/D는 앞 문장의 'however'와 '예측 vs 기록' 대조에 끌리는 그럴듯한 오답이고 B도 표면적으로 가능해 보여 비교가 필요함. 두 문장 간 관계를 정확히 읽어야 하므로 medium 적합. 해설 한·영 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 역사적 사실(1850 공공도서관법, 맨체스터 무료도서관 1852 개관)과 배경 설정이 모순되지 않음.

advisory.note: 근거에서 결론으로 이어지므로 Accordingly가 정답이다. 개혁가 예측과 실제 기록의 대조 때문에 Nevertheless와 In contrast가 그럴듯한 함정이 되어 medium 난이도에 맞는다. Manchester Free Library는 1852년에 개관했고 대출에서 소설 비중이 높았다는 서술은 대체로 사실과 부합한다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Falkirk Wheel, opened in Scotland in 2002, is a rotating boat lift that connects two canals.
- It lifts boats 24 meters, replacing a flight of 11 locks that once took most of a day to pass through.
- The wheel's two water-filled gondolas always balance each other, because a boat entering a gondola displaces its own weight in water.
- Because of this balance, turning the wheel requires only about 1.5 kilowatt-hours of electricity per half rotation.
- A half rotation takes about four minutes.

The student wants to explain why the Falkirk Wheel uses so little energy. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Falkirk Wheel, opened in Scotland in 2002, is a rotating boat lift that connects two canals.
- It lifts boats 24 meters, replacing a flight of 11 locks that once took most of a day to pass through.
- The wheel's two water-filled gondolas always balance each other, because a boat entering a gondola displaces its own weight in water.
- Because of this balance, turning the wheel requires only about 1.5 kilowatt-hours of electricity per half rotation.
- A half rotation takes about four minutes.
problem.question: The student wants to explain why the Falkirk Wheel uses so little energy. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Since a boat displaces its own weight in water, the Falkirk Wheel's two gondolas stay balanced, so a half rotation needs only about 1.5 kilowatt-hours of electricity.
The Falkirk Wheel needs only about 1.5 kilowatt-hours of electricity per half rotation, which takes about four minutes.
Opened in 2002, the Falkirk Wheel lifts boats 24 meters, replacing a flight of 11 locks that once took most of a day to pass through.
The Falkirk Wheel's two gondolas balance each other, allowing it to lift boats 24 meters in about four minutes rather than most of a day.
problem.explanation: 목표는 휠이 에너지를 적게 쓰는 '이유'를 설명하는 것이다. A는 배가 자기 무게만큼 물을 밀어내 곤돌라가 균형을 이룬다는 원인과 1.5kWh라는 결과를 연결하므로 정답이다. B는 적은 에너지 사용량은 제시하지만 그 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 개통 연도와 수문 대체 사실만 다루어 에너지와 무관하다. D는 균형을 언급하지만 이를 에너지가 아닌 속도와 연결해 목표에서 벗어난다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain why the wheel uses so little energy, so you need both a cause and the low-energy result. A links the cause (a boat displaces its own weight in water, keeping the gondolas balanced) to the result (only about 1.5 kilowatt-hours per half rotation), so A is correct. B states the low energy figure but never explains the reason for it. C covers the opening date and the replaced locks, which have nothing to do with energy. D mentions the balance but ties it to speed rather than energy use, so it misses the goal.

hardJudge.note: A는 원인(배가 자기 무게만큼 물을 밀어냄→곤돌라 균형)과 결과(반회전당 약 1.5kWh)를 명시적으로 연결해 '이유 설명' 목표를 충족한다. B는 에너지 수치만, D는 균형을 속도와 연결, C는 무관하여 각각 부분적 근거를 지니면서 배제된다. 팔커크 휠 관련 사실(2002년 개통, 24m, 11개 수문 대체, 반회전당 약 1.5kWh, 약 4분)은 공개된 정보와 부합한다. 한·영 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 중간 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: B(결과만 있음)와 D(균형을 속도와 연결)는 부분적으로 맞는 근거가 있는 매력적인 오답이고, C는 약하지만 말은 된다. 사실관계(24m, 11개 수문, 2002년, 1.5kWh)는 공개 자료와 일치한다. D는 노트에 없는 인과(균형→속도)를 만들어 내지만 오답이므로 문제없다.

problem.passage:
Hydroelectric dams along the upper Mekong River trap much of the sediment that once flowed downstream to the river's delta in southern Vietnam. Without that steady supply of silt, the delta can no longer rebuild the land that waves and tides wear away along its edges. ______ stretches of the delta's coastline have been retreating inland by several meters each year.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Hydroelectric dams along the upper Mekong River trap much of the sediment that once flowed downstream to the river's delta in southern Vietnam. Without that steady supply of silt, the delta can no longer rebuild the land that waves and tides wear away along its edges. ______ stretches of the delta's coastline have been retreating inland by several meters each year.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장들은 원인을 제시한다. 댐이 퇴적물을 가두고, 그 결과 삼각주가 침식된 땅을 다시 만들지 못한다. 마지막 문장의 해안선 후퇴는 이 원인에서 나온 결과이므로 인과를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 해안선 후퇴가 일반적 진술의 사례처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 앞 문장은 사례를 들 만한 일반화가 아니라 결과를 낳는 원인이다. B는 대조를 나타내는데 후퇴는 예상과 어긋나지 않고 오히려 예상과 맞아떨어진다. D는 비슷한 다른 현상을 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 후퇴는 별개의 유사 현상이 아니라 같은 과정의 결과이다.
problem.explanationEn: The first two sentences set up a cause: the dams trap sediment, so the delta can't rebuild land that erosion removes. The final sentence describes what happens because of this, which is the coastline retreating. That makes C, a cause-and-effect transition, the correct choice. A may seem plausible because the retreat sounds like an illustration, but the earlier sentences describe a cause that leads to a result, not a general claim that needs an example. B signals contrast, yet the retreat is exactly what you would expect, not something surprising. D adds a parallel, separate phenomenon, but the retreat is the outcome of the same process, not a similar one.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 댐→퇴적물 차단→삼각주 재건 불능→해안선 후퇴는 명확한 인과 사슬이므로 C(Consequently)가 정답. A는 '재건 불능'의 구체적 사례처럼 읽힐 수 있어 비교가 필요한 오답, D는 별개 유사 현상이 아니므로 배제, B는 대조가 아니므로 명백한 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 메콩 상류 댐의 퇴적물 차단과 삼각주 해안 침식(연 수 m 후퇴)은 사실에 부합. 원문 독창 텍스트로 저작권 의심 없음. 난이도는 표준 medium 수준 transitions 문항에 적합.

advisory.note: 인과 관계가 명확하다. 'For example'은 해안선 후퇴를 땅이 깎여 나가는 현상의 사례로 읽을 여지가 있어 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이다. 다소 쉬운 편이지만 medium 범위 안에 든다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The bombardier beetle (Brachinus) defends itself by spraying a hot chemical mixture at attackers.
- The beetle stores two harmless chemicals, hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide, in a reservoir in its abdomen.
- When threatened, it pushes these chemicals into a separate reaction chamber lined with enzymes.
- The enzymes trigger a rapid reaction that heats the mixture to about 100°C (212°F).
- The spray comes out in up to 500 pulses per second, and the beetle can aim it in nearly any direction.

The student wants to explain how the bombardier beetle produces its spray without harming itself. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The bombardier beetle (Brachinus) defends itself by spraying a hot chemical mixture at attackers.
- The beetle stores two harmless chemicals, hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide, in a reservoir in its abdomen.
- When threatened, it pushes these chemicals into a separate reaction chamber lined with enzymes.
- The enzymes trigger a rapid reaction that heats the mixture to about 100°C (212°F).
- The spray comes out in up to 500 pulses per second, and the beetle can aim it in nearly any direction.
problem.question: The student wants to explain how the bombardier beetle produces its spray without harming itself. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The bombardier beetle sprays a chemical mixture that reaches about 100°C, firing it in up to 500 pulses per second at attackers.
The bombardier beetle keeps two harmless chemicals in an abdominal reservoir and mixes them with enzymes only in a separate chamber when threatened, where they react and heat up to about 100°C.
When threatened, the bombardier beetle can aim its hot chemical spray in nearly any direction, making it an effective defense against attackers.
The bombardier beetle stores hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide in its abdomen, and its spray is released in rapid pulses of up to 500 per second.
problem.explanation: 목표는 딱정벌레가 스스로 다치지 않고 분사액을 만드는 방식을 설명하는 것이다. B는 무해한 화학물질을 저장소에 따로 두었다가 위협받을 때만 별도의 반응실에서 효소와 섞는다는 점을 연결해, 뜨거운 반응이 저장소와 떨어진 곳에서 일어난다는 것을 보여 준다. A는 온도와 분사 속도를 정확히 전하지만 자기 보호 방식은 설명하지 않는다. C는 조준 능력과 방어 효과만 강조한다. D는 저장되는 화학물질을 언급하지만 별도의 반응실과 효소 반응을 빠뜨려 왜 해가 없는지 설명하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain how the beetle makes its spray without hurting itself. B connects two notes: the beetle stores harmless chemicals in a reservoir, and it mixes them with enzymes only in a separate chamber when threatened. That shows the hot reaction happens away from where the chemicals are stored. A gives the temperature and pulse rate correctly, but it says nothing about how the beetle protects itself. C focuses only on aiming and how well the defense works. D names the stored chemicals but leaves out the separate chamber and the enzyme reaction, so it doesn't explain why the beetle stays safe.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검증 완료: 목표(자신을 해치지 않고 분사액 생성)에 맞게 '무해한 화학물질을 저장소에 보관' + '별도 반응실에서 효소와 반응' 두 노트를 연결한 유일한 선택지. A(온도·펄스), D(저장 물질·펄스)는 노트 사실을 정확히 담아 부분적 근거를 가지나 분리 저장·별도 반응실 메커니즘이 빠져 배제되고, C는 조준·방어 효과만 다루어 말이 되지만 목표와 어긋남. 과학적 사실(하이드로퀴논+과산화수소, ~100°C, 최대 500펄스/초, Brachinus) 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 형식 적합, 저작권 의심 없음. 두 노트 연결 + 목표 대조 필요로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 B만 '무해한 화학물질 저장 + 별도 반응실'을 포함하고 자기 보호 메커니즘을 드러냄. 오답 A·C는 자기 보호와 무관함이 즉시 보이고, D만 부분적 근거(저장)를 가짐. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져야 한다는 기준에 못 미쳐 훑어 읽어도 정답 도출 가능함. 또한 B만 유독 길어 길이 단서가 있음. 사실관계(하이드로퀴논·과산화수소, 약 100°C, 초당 약 500회 펄스)는 문헌과 부합함.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lake Balkhash, in eastern Kazakhstan, stretches about 600 kilometers from west to east.
- A narrow strait divides the lake into a western half and an eastern half.
- The western half is fed mainly by the Ili River, which carries fresh water from mountains in China.
- The western half's water is nearly fresh and is used for drinking by nearby communities.
- The eastern half receives little river inflow, and its water is salty.
- Scientists attribute the salinity difference to how little water flows through the narrow strait between the two halves.

The student wants to contrast the water in the two halves of Lake Balkhash. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lake Balkhash, in eastern Kazakhstan, stretches about 600 kilometers from west to east.
- A narrow strait divides the lake into a western half and an eastern half.
- The western half is fed mainly by the Ili River, which carries fresh water from mountains in China.
- The western half's water is nearly fresh and is used for drinking by nearby communities.
- The eastern half receives little river inflow, and its water is salty.
- Scientists attribute the salinity difference to how little water flows through the narrow strait between the two halves.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast the water in the two halves of Lake Balkhash. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Lake Balkhash, which stretches about 600 kilometers across eastern Kazakhstan, is divided by a narrow strait into a western half and an eastern half.
The western half of Lake Balkhash is fed mainly by the Ili River, which carries fresh water from mountains in China, and nearby communities use it for drinking.
Scientists attribute differences within Lake Balkhash to how little water flows through the narrow strait that divides the lake into two halves.
Although the western half of Lake Balkhash is nearly fresh, the eastern half, which receives little river inflow, holds salty water.
problem.explanation: 목표는 호수 두 부분의 물을 대조하는 것이므로 서쪽(거의 담수)과 동쪽(염수)을 함께 제시해야 한다. D는 'Although'로 두 부분의 물 성질을 직접 대조하므로 정답이다. A는 호수가 두 부분으로 나뉜다는 사실만 말하고 물의 차이는 언급하지 않는다. B는 서쪽 절반의 물만 설명해 대조가 없다. C는 차이의 원인을 말하지만 각 절반의 물이 어떻게 다른지는 밝히지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to contrast the water in the two halves, so the sentence needs to describe both halves and show how they differ. D does this: it uses "Although" to set the nearly fresh western half against the salty eastern half. A only says the lake is divided into two halves and never mentions how their water differs. B describes only the western half, so nothing is being contrasted. C explains why there is a difference but never says what the difference is (fresh water versus salty water).

hardJudge.note: D는 'Although'로 서쪽(거의 담수)과 동쪽(염수)의 물을 직접 대조하여 목표를 충족. A는 지리적 구분만, B는 서쪽만, C는 원인만 제시해 대조 불성립. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조 일치, 모순 없음. 발하슈호 사실관계(길이 약 600km, 일리강 유입, 서쪽 담수/동쪽 염수, 좁은 해협) 정확. C가 '차이·해협'을 언급해 그럴듯하고 B도 '담수'를 포함해 부분적 근거가 있어 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: D는 'western half is nearly fresh'로 호수 절반 자체를 fresh라고 표현해 다소 어색하지만(물이 담수) 수용 가능. 오답 A·C는 두 절반/차이를 언급해 부분적 매력이 있고 B는 한쪽만 다뤄 표준 medium에 부합.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lift bridges allow ships to pass beneath them by raising a movable section of roadway.
- In a vertical-lift bridge, the movable span stays level and rises straight up between two towers.
- The Aerial Lift Bridge in Duluth, Minnesota, completed in its current form in 1929, is a vertical-lift bridge whose span rises about 135 feet.
- In a bascule bridge, the movable span pivots upward at one end, tilting like a seesaw.
- Chicago's DuSable Bridge, opened in 1920, is a bascule bridge whose two leaves tilt up from the riverbanks.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in how the movable spans of the two bridges operate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lift bridges allow ships to pass beneath them by raising a movable section of roadway.
- In a vertical-lift bridge, the movable span stays level and rises straight up between two towers.
- The Aerial Lift Bridge in Duluth, Minnesota, completed in its current form in 1929, is a vertical-lift bridge whose span rises about 135 feet.
- In a bascule bridge, the movable span pivots upward at one end, tilting like a seesaw.
- Chicago's DuSable Bridge, opened in 1920, is a bascule bridge whose two leaves tilt up from the riverbanks.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how the movable spans of the two bridges operate. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Aerial Lift Bridge in Duluth was completed in its current form in 1929, nine years after Chicago's DuSable Bridge opened in 1920.
Whereas the span of Duluth's Aerial Lift Bridge stays level as it rises straight up between two towers, the leaves of Chicago's DuSable Bridge tilt upward from the riverbanks.
Both Duluth's Aerial Lift Bridge and Chicago's DuSable Bridge allow ships to pass beneath them by raising a movable section of roadway.
Chicago's DuSable Bridge is a bascule bridge, a type in which the movable span pivots upward at one end, tilting like a seesaw.
problem.explanation: 목표는 두 다리의 가동 구간이 작동하는 방식의 '차이'를 강조하는 것이다. B는 Duluth 다리의 구간은 수평을 유지한 채 곧게 올라가고 DuSable 다리는 기울어 올라간다는 점을 대조하므로 정답이다. A는 두 다리를 대조하지만 작동 방식이 아니라 완공 연도의 차이를 다룬다. C는 차이가 아닌 공통점을 강조한다. D는 작동 방식을 정확히 설명하지만 한 다리만 다루어 차이를 보여 주지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The goal is to emphasize a difference in how the two bridges' movable spans operate. B contrasts the Duluth span, which stays level and rises straight up, with the DuSable leaves, which tilt upward, so it is correct. A does compare the two bridges, but the difference it points out is their completion dates, not how they operate. C emphasizes something the bridges have in common rather than a difference. D accurately describes how a span works, but it covers only one bridge, so it doesn't show a contrast.

hardJudge.note: B만이 두 다리의 가동 구간 작동 방식(수평 상승 vs. 기울어짐)을 대조함. A는 두 다리 대조이나 연도 차이, D는 작동 방식이나 한 다리만, C는 공통점 — 각 오답이 목표의 일부 요소를 충족해 비교가 필요한 medium 구조. 노트 사실(Aerial Lift Bridge 1929 수직 승강 개조·약 135ft, DuSable 1920 이중 leaf 바스큘)도 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조 일치.

advisory.note: 표준 SAT 형식이다. A는 대조(차이)라는 근거, C는 작동 방식이라는 근거, D는 작동 방식의 정확성이라는 근거를 부분적으로 갖추고 있어 medium 난이도에 맞다. 팩트도 확인했다: Aerial Lift Bridge는 1929년 개축, 약 135ft 상승이고 DuSable Bridge는 1920년 개통이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lake Chad is a freshwater lake located where Chad, Cameroon, Niger, and Nigeria meet.
- In the 1960s, the lake covered roughly 25,000 square kilometers.
- By the late 1980s, its surface area had shrunk to about 1,350 square kilometers.
- Researchers attribute the decline to prolonged drought and increased irrigation withdrawals.
- Lake Baikal, in Siberia, holds about 20 percent of Earth's unfrozen surface fresh water.
- Unlike Lake Chad, Lake Baikal has remained relatively stable in volume over the same period.

The student wants to emphasize the scale of Lake Chad's change over time. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lake Chad is a freshwater lake located where Chad, Cameroon, Niger, and Nigeria meet.
- In the 1960s, the lake covered roughly 25,000 square kilometers.
- By the late 1980s, its surface area had shrunk to about 1,350 square kilometers.
- Researchers attribute the decline to prolonged drought and increased irrigation withdrawals.
- Lake Baikal, in Siberia, holds about 20 percent of Earth's unfrozen surface fresh water.
- Unlike Lake Chad, Lake Baikal has remained relatively stable in volume over the same period.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize the scale of Lake Chad's change over time. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Lake Chad, which covered roughly 25,000 square kilometers in the 1960s, had shrunk to about 1,350 square kilometers by the late 1980s.
Lake Chad has declined in size due to prolonged drought and increased irrigation withdrawals, according to researchers.
While Lake Chad's surface area changed dramatically after the 1960s, Lake Baikal remained relatively stable in volume.
Located where Chad, Cameroon, Niger, and Nigeria meet, Lake Chad covered roughly 25,000 square kilometers in the 1960s.
problem.explanation: 목표는 차드호 변화의 '규모'를 강조하는 것이므로 두 시점의 면적(약 25,000㎢→약 1,350㎢)을 함께 제시해야 한다. A는 두 수치를 결합해 급격한 감소 폭을 분명히 보여준다. B는 감소의 원인을 설명할 뿐 얼마나 줄었는지 규모를 제시하지 않는다. C는 바이칼호와의 대조에 초점을 두며 '극적으로'라고만 할 뿐 구체적 규모가 없다. D는 1960년대 면적 하나만 있어 변화 자체가 드러나지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to emphasize the scale of Lake Chad's change, so you need both the earlier and later surface areas (about 25,000 km² and about 1,350 km²). A combines these two figures, making the size of the drop clear. B explains why the lake shrank but never shows how much it shrank. C focuses on a contrast with Lake Baikal and only calls the change "dramatic" without giving its scale. D gives just the 1960s area, so no change over time is shown at all.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 두 시점 수치를 결합해 변화 규모를 직접 보여주며 유일하게 목표를 충족. B(원인), C(바이칼호 대조, '극적으로'라는 표현으로 부분적 근거 보유), D(단일 시점 수치)는 각각 노트 정보를 사용하지만 규모를 보여주지 못함. 해설 한·영 일치, 선택지 참조 정확. 노트의 사실(차드호 1960년대 약 25,000㎢→1980년대 약 1,350㎢, 바이칼호 약 20% 담수)은 통상 인용되는 수치와 부합. 표준 SAT 수사적 종합 문항 중간 난이도에 적합.

A only describes what the lakes have in common (both are endorheic and both shrank) and never mentions causes. C gives Lake Chad's cause but leaves out the Aral Sea, so there's no comparison at all. D stresses a similarity with "Like" and gives only the Aral Sea's cause.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산: 'Whereas'로 아랄해(관개용 하천 전환)와 차드호(가뭄+물 사용 증가)의 원인을 대조하여 목표(원인의 차이 강조)를 정확히 달성. D describes the closing process but leaves out the point that ships can pass freely the rest of the time.

hardJudge.note: C는 '평소 도크에 있어 수로 개방'과 '해일 시 폐쇄'를 모두 연결해 목표를 충족. D는 작동 과정만, B는 비교만, A는 건설 정보만 다루어 배제됨. 노트 사실(1991–1997, 210m, 템스 배리어 1982, 회전식 수문) 정확. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. D·B가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: B와 D가 각각 부분적 근거(도크 보관, 해일 시 작동)를 가져 비교가 필요함. 사실관계(1991–1997, 약 210m, 템스 배리어 1982)도 맞음. 형식 적합.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Arctic tern and the bar-tailed godwit are both long-distance migratory shorebirds.
- The Arctic tern travels roughly 70,000 kilometers each year, stopping repeatedly to feed along its route.
- In 2022, a tagged bar-tailed godwit flew about 13,560 kilometers from Alaska to Tasmania.
- The godwit completed that flight in 11 days without landing once.
- Before migrating, godwits shrink some digestive organs and store fat to fuel nonstop flight.

The student wants to contrast the migration strategies of the two birds. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Arctic tern and the bar-tailed godwit are both long-distance migratory shorebirds.
- The Arctic tern travels roughly 70,000 kilometers each year, stopping repeatedly to feed along its route.
- In 2022, a tagged bar-tailed godwit flew about 13,560 kilometers from Alaska to Tasmania.
- The godwit completed that flight in 11 days without landing once.
- Before migrating, godwits shrink some digestive organs and store fat to fuel nonstop flight.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast the migration strategies of the two birds. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the Arctic tern breaks its roughly 70,000-kilometer annual journey with repeated feeding stops, one bar-tailed godwit flew about 13,560 kilometers in 11 days without landing once.
In 2022, a tagged bar-tailed godwit flew about 13,560 kilometers from Alaska to Tasmania in 11 days, never landing once during the flight.
The bar-tailed godwit, which flew about 13,560 kilometers in 2022, prepares for migration by shrinking some digestive organs and storing fat for its journey.
Although the Arctic tern travels roughly 70,000 kilometers a year, it flies more slowly than the bar-tailed godwit, which covered about 13,560 kilometers nonstop in 11 days.
problem.explanation: 목표는 두 새의 이동 '전략'을 대조하는 것이다. A는 제비갈매기의 '반복적 먹이 섭취 정지'와 큰뒷부리도요의 '무착륙 비행'이라는 서로 다른 두 사실을 whereas로 결합해 전략 차이를 드러낸다. B는 도요 한쪽 사실만 담아 대조가 없다. C는 두 사실(비행 거리와 신체 준비)을 결합했지만 모두 도요에 관한 것이라 두 새의 대조라는 목표와 무관하다. D는 노트에 없는 '제비갈매기가 더 느리게 난다'는 비교를 덧붙여 사실을 왜곡하며, 전략이 아닌 속도를 대조한다.
problem.explanationEn: The goal is to contrast the two birds' migration strategies. Choice A joins two separate facts with "whereas": the tern stops repeatedly to feed, while the godwit flew without landing even once. That sets the two strategies directly against each other. Choice B describes only the godwit, so nothing is being contrasted. Choice C combines two facts, but both are about the godwit (its flight distance and how it prepares), so it doesn't compare the two birds. Choice D says the tern flies more slowly, which the notes never state. It also contrasts speed instead of strategy.

hardJudge.note: A는 제비갈매기의 '반복 급식 정지'와 도요의 '무착륙 비행'을 whereas로 결합해 '전략' 대조라는 목표를 정확히 충족. B는 도요 한쪽만, C는 두 사실 모두 도요 관련으로 대조 부재, D는 노트에 없는 속도 비교('더 느리게')를 삽입하고 전략이 아닌 속도를 대조해 범위 이탈. D가 접속어와 대조 구조를 갖춘 매력적 오답이라 단순 사실 선택을 넘어 목표 범위(전략 vs 속도/거리) 판별과 노트 근거 확인을 요구함. 수치(70,000km, 13,560km/11일 2022 기록)도 실제 사실과 부합.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞다. 다만 한쪽 새만 다루는 B·C는 바로 탈락하고, 두 새를 모두 다루는 D는 노트에 없는 '더 느리다'는 주장이 드러나 있어 쉽게 걸러진다. 그래서 문항은 전형적인 medium 수준의 대조 문항이다. 그럴듯하지만 미묘하게 어긋나는 대조 오답(예: 거리만 대조하는 선택지)이 없어서, 목표 범위를 따져 보거나 관계 방향을 판별하는 hard 특성이 실제로 요구되지 않는다.

problem.passage:
When marine biologist Ayana Okafor began tagging juvenile green sea turtles off the coast of Ghana in 2014, her goal was not to estimate how many turtles lived there but to trace the routes they traveled between feeding grounds. Her tags logged water temperature and depth along with location, and over six years the dataset grew to tens of thousands of readings. Many of those temperature readings have since proved valuable to oceanographers studying coastal warming. ______ Okafor herself has published almost exclusively on the turtles' movement corridors, treating the temperature records as a by-product of her tracking work.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When marine biologist Ayana Okafor began tagging juvenile green sea turtles off the coast of Ghana in 2014, her goal was not to estimate how many turtles lived there but to trace the routes they traveled between feeding grounds. Her tags logged water temperature and depth along with location, and over six years the dataset grew to tens of thousands of readings. Many of those temperature readings have since proved valuable to oceanographers studying coastal warming. ______ Okafor herself has published almost exclusively on the turtles' movement corridors, treating the temperature records as a by-product of her tracking work.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation:
정답 D(Even so,). 지문의 핵심은 Okafor의 '의도'가 개체 수가 아니라 이동 경로 추적이었다는 점이다. 바로 앞 문장은 온도 데이터가 해양학자들에게 가치 있었다는 부수적 결과를 말하고, 마지막 문장은 그럼에도 Okafor 본인은 원래 의도대로 이동 경로에만 집중했다고 말한다. 따라서 앞 문장에서 기대되는 바(온도 연구로 확장)와 실제를 대비하는 양보 전환어가 맞다.
A(Accordingly,)는 앞 문장의 결과(온도 데이터의 유용성)에 맞춰 이어 붙인 오답이다. '그에 따라'라면 그녀가 온도 연구를 했어야 하는데 실제로는 반대다.
B(Likewise,)는 Okafor와 해양학자가 모두 데이터를 연구했다는 점에서 방향은 비슷해 보이지만, 두 사람의 초점이 다르므로 유사 관계는 성립하지 않는다.
C(For instance,)는 마지막 문장을 앞 문장 주장(해양학자들에게 유용함)의 예시로 연결하는데, Okafor의 연구는 온도 데이터를 활용한 사례가 아니므로 전혀 다른 내용과 이어진다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is D (Even so,). The passage stresses Okafor's intent: she wanted to trace the turtles' routes, not count them. The sentence right before the blank describes a side benefit, since oceanographers found her temperature data valuable. The last sentence says that she herself still wrote almost only about movement corridors. You might expect the temperature data's usefulness to pull her toward warming research, but it didn't. That makes this a concession/contrast, so "Even so" fits.
A (Accordingly) picks up on the side benefit in the previous sentence. It suggests that her publishing followed from that usefulness, but she actually did the opposite.
B (Likewise) seems close because both Okafor and the oceanographers used the data. But their focus was different, so "similarly" isn't the right relationship.
C (For instance) makes the last sentence an example of oceanographers using the temperature data. Okafor's work isn't such an example, so this transition links to the wrong idea.

hardJudge.note: 직접 검산: 앞 문장(온도 데이터가 해양학자에게 유용) → 마지막 문장(Okafor 본인은 이동 경로에만 집중, 온도 기록은 부산물)은 기대와 실제의 양보·대조 관계이므로 'Even so'가 유일하게 성립. A는 인과 방향 오류(유용했으니 온도 연구를 했어야 함), B는 유사 관계 불성립, C는 예시 관계 불성립. 첫 문장의 '목적(경로 추적) vs 결과(온도 데이터 가치)' 구분을 파악해야 하며 'herself'가 단서로 작동하는 구조가 goal_vs_content 변별을 요구함. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 설명하고 모순 없음. 지문은 가상의 연구자로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 바로 앞 문장(다른 연구자들에게 온도 데이터가 유용했다)과 빈칸 뒤 문장(본인은 이동 경로만 다뤘다) 사이의 양보 관계만 보면 Even so가 바로 정해진다. 첫 문장의 목적 정보(개체 수 추정이 아니라 경로 추적)는 정답 선택에 사실상 필요하지 않다. 따라서 goal_vs_content 판별이 실제로 작동하지 않는 전형적인 medium 수준의 양보 전환 문항이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Marine biologist Lena Ortiz studied hermit crabs on a rocky shore in Baja California.
- In a laboratory tank, she confirmed that the crabs can detect the chemical odor released by dead snails, which leave behind empty shells.
- When the odor was added to the tank, every crab moved toward its source within two minutes.
- In the field, Ortiz observed that crabs gathered near dead snails more often than near living ones.
- She suggested that the crabs may use this odor to locate newly vacated shells, though she noted that the field pattern could have other explanations, such as crabs scavenging the snails' flesh.

The student wants to present both what Ortiz established and what she only proposed, accurately reflecting the certainty of each. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Marine biologist Lena Ortiz studied hermit crabs on a rocky shore in Baja California.
- In a laboratory tank, she confirmed that the crabs can detect the chemical odor released by dead snails, which leave behind empty shells.
- When the odor was added to the tank, every crab moved toward its source within two minutes.
- In the field, Ortiz observed that crabs gathered near dead snails more often than near living ones.
- She suggested that the crabs may use this odor to locate newly vacated shells, though she noted that the field pattern could have other explanations, such as crabs scavenging the snails' flesh.
problem.question: The student wants to present both what Ortiz established and what she only proposed, accurately reflecting the certainty of each. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ortiz demonstrated that hermit crabs can detect the odor of dead snails, and her field observations proved that the crabs use this odor to find newly vacated shells.
Ortiz's work suggests that hermit crabs might be able to detect the odor of dead snails, and it is possible that the crabs use this odor to find newly vacated shells.
Ortiz showed that hermit crabs can detect the odor of dead snails; she proposed, though not conclusively, that the crabs use this odor to find newly vacated shells.
Ortiz showed that hermit crabs gather near dead snails more often than near living ones; she proposed, though not conclusively, that the crabs move toward the odor within two minutes.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 실험실에서 '확인된(confirmed)' 냄새 감지 능력은 확정적으로(showed), 빈 껍데기를 찾는 데 냄새를 쓴다는 것은 Ortiz가 '제안했고(suggested)' 다른 설명도 가능하다고 했으므로 잠정적으로(proposed, though not conclusively) 서술했다.
A: 현장 관찰은 다른 설명(사체 먹기)이 가능하다고 했는데 'proved'라고 해 잠정적 가설을 확정으로 과장했다.
B: 냄새 감지는 실험으로 확인된 사실인데 'might be able to'로 불필요하게 낮췄다.
D: '확정 + 잠정' 구조는 맞지만, 잠정적 내용 자리에 실험에서 실제로 관찰된 2분 내 이동을 넣었고 Ortiz의 실제 가설(껍데기 찾기)은 빠졌다. 서로 다른 연구 내용을 뒤섞었다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: Ortiz confirmed in the lab that the crabs detect the odor, so "showed" fits. Her idea that the crabs use the odor to find shells was only a suggestion, and she admitted other explanations were possible, so "proposed, though not conclusively" fits that part.
A: The field pattern could have other explanations, such as scavenging. Saying it "proved" the shell-finding idea overstates a tentative claim.
B: Odor detection was confirmed in the lab, so "might be able to" makes an established fact sound uncertain when it isn't.
D: This answer has the right structure, with one established claim and one tentative claim, but it uses the wrong content. The two-minute movement was a measured lab result, not Ortiz's proposal. It also leaves out her actual hypothesis about finding shells.

hardJudge.note: 노트는 실험실 확인(confirmed, 2분 내 전원 이동)이라는 확정 진술과 'suggested… could have other explanations'라는 잠정 진술을 명확히 구분해 제시함. C는 전자를 showed, 후자를 proposed, though not conclusively로 정확히 매핑. A는 proved로 과잉 확정(과잉 일반화), B는 확인된 사실을 might be able to로 과도 축소, D는 확정/잠정 구조는 맞지만 실험에서 관찰된 사실(2분 내 이동)을 잠정 자리에 넣고 실제 가설을 누락해 내용 배치 오류. 정답 유일성 확보, 해설과 선택지 논리 일치. 가상의 연구자이며 집게류의 복족류 사체 냄새 감지는 실제 연구와도 부합하여 사실 오류 없음.

advisory.note: C가 유일하게 옳다(확정적 실험 결과 + 단서를 단 가설). A는 과잉 일반화, B는 확실성을 지나치게 낮췄고, D는 확실성 위치를 잘못 배치했다. 단어 하나(proved, might)만 보고 고를 수 있는 오답이 있어 난이도는 중상 수준이며, hard 하한에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
Ecologist Mariana Okafor observed that wild side-blotched lizards in the Mojave Desert become noticeably less active during the hottest hours of summer afternoons, retreating into burrows until evening. In laboratory enclosures, however, the same species consistently chose to rest directly beneath heat lamps, moving away from cooler corners whenever given the option. ______ Okafor concluded that the lizards are neither drawn to nor repelled by heat as such; rather, they move in whatever direction keeps their bodies within a narrow preferred temperature range.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Ecologist Mariana Okafor observed that wild side-blotched lizards in the Mojave Desert become noticeably less active during the hottest hours of summer afternoons, retreating into burrows until evening. In laboratory enclosures, however, the same species consistently chose to rest directly beneath heat lamps, moving away from cooler corners whenever given the option. ______ Okafor concluded that the lizards are neither drawn to nor repelled by heat as such; rather, they move in whatever direction keeps their bodies within a narrow preferred temperature range.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 야생에서는 더위를 피하고 실험실에서는 열을 찾는 상반된 듯한 두 관찰을 함께 고려하면, 도마뱀은 열 자체가 아니라 일정한 체온 범위를 추구한다는 결론이 나온다. 'Considering both findings'가 두 관찰을 종합해 결론을 끌어내는 관계를 정확히 나타낸다. B(Nevertheless): 앞뒤가 대립한다고만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 마지막 문장은 두 관찰에 맞서는 내용이 아니라 두 관찰을 모두 설명하는 결론이다. C(In other words): 바로 앞의 실험실 관찰만 다시 말하는 표현이라 한쪽 관찰만 반영한다. 결론은 '열에 끌리지 않는다'고 말하므로 앞 문장을 바꿔 말한 것이 아니다. D(For instance): 마지막 문장은 앞 내용의 예시가 아니라 일반화된 결론이므로 종합 결론과 관계없는 전환어다.
problem.explanationEn: The right answer is A. In the wild, the lizards avoid the afternoon heat. In the lab, they look for heat. These two observations seem to clash, but the last sentence explains both: the lizards are after a specific body temperature range, not heat itself. "Considering both findings" shows that the conclusion comes from putting the two observations together. B ("Nevertheless") treats the last sentence as a simple contrast, but the conclusion doesn't push back against the observations. It explains both of them. C ("In other words") would mean the last sentence just restates the lab finding. That's only one side, and the conclusion actually says the lizards are not drawn to heat as such. D ("For instance") would make the last sentence an example, but it's actually a general conclusion.

hardJudge.note: 야생(열 회피)과 실험실(열 추구)의 상반된 관찰을 종합해 '체온 범위 유지'라는 결론으로 잇는 구조가 명확하며, 정답 A만 종합 관계를 표현한다. B는 단순 대조, C는 직전 문장 재진술(한쪽 관찰만 반영), D는 예시로 모두 배제 가능. 해설의 각 오답 설명이 지문과 일치하고 모순 없음. 'Considering both findings,'가 전형적 SAT 전환어보다 다소 서술적이지만 형식상 허용 범위. 결론 문장 자체에 'rather'가 있어 'In other words'가 매력적 오답으로 기능하며, 표면 대조를 넘어 종합 추론을 요구하므로 hard 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 'Considering both findings'가 두 관찰을 종합한다는 사실을 문자 그대로 드러내고 있어, 지문의 'both'·결론 구조와 표면적으로만 맞춰 봐도 답을 고를 수 있음. 오답 D는 명백히 어색하고 C도 쉽게 제거됨. 실제 SAT 정답 선택지에서도 보기 드문 설명형 전환어라서 hard 수준의 변별력이 부족함.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lichens are partnerships between a fungus and a photosynthetic partner, usually an alga.
- The map lichen (Rhizocarpon geographicum) grows on exposed rock in mountain regions.
- In the Swiss Alps, map lichen colonies grow outward at roughly 0.5 millimeters per year.
- Elegant sunburst lichen (Xanthoria elegans) is also found on alpine rock surfaces.
- In the same region, elegant sunburst lichen colonies grow outward at roughly 3 millimeters per year.
- Because of its slow, steady growth, map lichen is used by geologists to estimate how long rock surfaces have been exposed.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in growth rate between the two lichens. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Lichens are partnerships between a fungus and a photosynthetic partner, usually an alga.
- The map lichen (Rhizocarpon geographicum) grows on exposed rock in mountain regions.
- In the Swiss Alps, map lichen colonies grow outward at roughly 0.5 millimeters per year.
- Elegant sunburst lichen (Xanthoria elegans) is also found on alpine rock surfaces.
- In the same region, elegant sunburst lichen colonies grow outward at roughly 3 millimeters per year.
- Because of its slow, steady growth, map lichen is used by geologists to estimate how long rock surfaces have been exposed.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize a difference in growth rate between the two lichens. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Map lichen colonies in the Swiss Alps grow outward at only about 0.5 millimeters per year, a pace slow and steady enough that geologists use the lichen to date exposed rock surfaces.

Whereas map lichen colonies in the Swiss Alps expand by only about 0.5 millimeters per year, elegant sunburst lichen colonies in the same region spread roughly six times faster, at about 3 millimeters per year.
Both map lichen and elegant sunburst lichen grow on exposed alpine rock, and each is a partnership between a fungus and a photosynthetic partner such as an alga.
Elegant sunburst lichen grows about 3 millimeters per year, six times faster than map lichen, which is why geologists prefer it over map lichen for dating rock surfaces.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 두 지의류의 성장률(0.5mm vs 3mm, 같은 지역)을 대조 접속사 whereas로 결합해 성장 속도 차이를 강조한다. 6배는 노트 수치로 바로 도출된다.
A: 지도 지의류의 성장률만 담아 비교 대상이 없으므로 목표를 절반만 달성한다.
C: 두 지의류에 관한 사실을 결합했지만 서식지·공생 구조의 공통점이라 성장률 차이라는 목표와 무관하다.
D: 노트에 따르면 지질학자는 느리고 꾸준한 지도 지의류를 연대 측정에 쓴다. 선버스트 지의류를 선호한다는 내용은 노트에 없고 사실을 왜곡한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice B is the best answer. It brings together the two growth rates (0.5 mm versus 3 mm per year, both measured in the same region) and links them with the contrast word "whereas," so the difference in growth rate is front and center. The "six times faster" figure follows directly from the numbers in the notes.
Choice A gives only the map lichen's rate. Without a second lichen to compare against, it shows no difference, so it does just half the job.
Choice C combines facts about both lichens, but those facts are things they have in common (where they grow and what they're made of), not their growth rates, so it doesn't meet the goal.
Choice D contradicts the notes. The notes say geologists use the slow-growing map lichen for dating. Nothing in them says geologists prefer elegant sunburst lichen.

hardJudge.note: B가 유일하게 두 지의류의 성장률(0.5mm vs 3mm, 동일 지역)을 대조 구조로 결합해 목표를 충족. A는 한쪽 사실만, C는 성장률과 무관한 공통점, D는 노트에 없는(그리고 노트와 모순되는) 지질학자 선호 주장을 포함. 6배 수치는 3/0.5=6으로 정확. D는 수치는 맞되 인과 방향을 왜곡해 relation_direction_judgment를 요구하고, C는 '관련 있는 두 사실 결합'이지만 목표 초점이 어긋나 purpose_scope_calibration을 시험함. 전형적 medium(단일 사실 선택)보다 추가 사고 요구. 사실관계(지의류 공생, Rhizocarpon geographicum의 lichenometry 활용, 성장률 대략치) 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 B만 두 성장률을 대비하며 6배(3/0.5)도 정확하다. 다만 '차이를 강조'하는 목표에서 두 수치를 대조하는 전형적인 medium 구조이다. D는 지질학자 관련 내용을 왜곡해 쉽게 제거되고, A는 한쪽 사실만, C는 목표와 무관한 내용이라 오답이 명백하다. 확실성 구분, 관계 방향 판별, 배경 정보 위계 같은 hard 특성이 요구되지 않는다.

problem.passage:
Ecologist Mariana Ruiz recorded how often managed honeybees and wild bumblebees visited blueberry flowers on a farm in southern Chile. Honeybees landed on the flowers far more often than the bumblebees did. ______ each bumblebee visit left roughly four times as much pollen on a flower's stigma as a honeybee visit, a difference Ruiz links to the bumblebees' habit of vibrating their bodies to shake pollen loose.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Ecologist Mariana Ruiz recorded how often managed honeybees and wild bumblebees visited blueberry flowers on a farm in southern Chile. Honeybees landed on the flowers far more often than the bumblebees did. ______ each bumblebee visit left roughly four times as much pollen on a flower's stigma as a honeybee visit, a difference Ruiz links to the bumblebees' habit of vibrating their bodies to shake pollen loose.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation:
정답 A(However). 두 번째 문장에서 더 자주 방문한 것은 주어인 꿀벌(Honeybees)이고, 'than the bumblebees did'는 비교 대상일 뿐이다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 반대로 호박벌이 방문 1회당 꽃가루를 약 4배 더 남긴다고 말한다. 따라서 '횟수는 꿀벌이 많다'와 '1회당 효율은 호박벌이 높다'가 대조를 이루므로 However가 알맞다.
B(Moreover): 문장 끝의 인접 명사 bumblebees를 '더 자주 방문한' 주체로 잘못 읽으면 '호박벌이 더 자주 방문하고, 게다가 더 많이 남긴다'처럼 정보가 덧붙는 관계로 보인다. 하지만 실제로 더 자주 방문한 쪽은 꿀벌이므로 틀리다.
C(Similarly): 문장은 문법적으로 자연스럽게 이어지지만, 두 문장은 서로 다른 벌이 서로 다른 기준에서 우세하다는 내용이므로 유사 관계가 성립하지 않는다.
D(As a result): 꿀벌의 잦은 방문을 원인으로 보고 꽃가루 양을 그 결과로 연결하는 선택지이다. 그러나 꽃가루를 많이 남기는 쪽은 호박벌이고, 지문은 그 이유를 몸을 진동시키는 습성에서 찾으므로 인과 관계가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer: A (However). In the second sentence, the subject Honeybees is what lands "far more often." The phrase "than the bumblebees did" only names what honeybees are compared to. The next sentence says the opposite kind of thing: each bumblebee visit leaves about four times as much pollen. Honeybees lead in number of visits, while bumblebees lead in pollen per visit, so the sentences contrast and "However" fits.
B (Moreover) works only if you take the nearby noun "bumblebees" as the group that visited more often. Then the second fact would seem to add another advantage for bumblebees. But honeybees, not bumblebees, made more visits.
C (Similarly) sounds smooth, but the two sentences don't describe similar facts. Each describes a different bee winning on a different measure.
D (As a result) treats the honeybees' frequent visits as the cause of the pollen amount. But it's the bumblebees that leave more pollen, and the text credits their vibrating behavior, not the honeybees' visits.

hardJudge.note: 두 번째 문장의 비교 구문 'than the bumblebees did'에서 실제 우세 주체는 문두의 Honeybees이며, 문장 끝 인접 명사 bumblebees를 주체로 오독하면 Moreover가 그럴듯해지도록 설계됨. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 '방문 횟수(꿀벌 우세)' 대 '방문당 꽃가루량(호박벌 우세)'이라는 서로 다른 기준의 대조이므로 However가 유일한 정답. Similarly/As a result는 문법적으로 자연스럽지만 논리적으로 성립하지 않음. 해설의 각 오답 분석도 지문과 정확히 일치. 호박벌의 진동 수분(buzz pollination)으로 블루베리 꽃에 더 많은 꽃가루를 남긴다는 사실도 생태학적으로 타당. 세 번째 문장이 동격구로 다소 길지만 구조 자체는 단순하여 체크리스트 5 충족으로 판단. 단, 주어가 문두에 명시된 전형적 비교문이라 지시 대상 추적 난도는 중간 수준이며, hard 특성은 '빈도 vs 효율'이라는 기준 차이를 식별해야 하는 점에서 주로 확보됨.

advisory.note: 정답 However는 맞다. 다만 지시 대상이 떨어져 있다는 설계가 실제로는 작동하지 않는다. 'Honeybees landed ... far more often than the bumblebees did'에서 주어 Honeybees는 문장 맨 앞에 있어 바로 보이고, than 비교 구문도 표준적이다. 그래서 인접 명사 bumblebees를 주체로 잘못 읽을 가능성이 낮다. 결국 '빈도 대 1회당 효율'을 대조하는 전형적인 medium 수준의 However 문항이며, hard의 non_local_referent_tracking을 실제로 요구하지 않는다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Okafor studied hummingbirds visiting feeders at 40 mountain sites in Colombia.
- She confirmed through banding records that individual birds returned to the same feeder sites across three consecutive years.
- She also found that sites with more flowering shrubs nearby tended to have higher return rates, though the pattern varied considerably from site to site.
- Okafor cautions that this association may reflect other site features, such as elevation, rather than the shrubs themselves.
- In a separate study, botanist Lien Tran showed that hummingbirds visiting shrub flowers increased seed production in those shrubs.

The student wants to present both of Okafor's findings while accurately reflecting how strongly each is supported. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ecologist Mariana Okafor studied hummingbirds visiting feeders at 40 mountain sites in Colombia.
- She confirmed through banding records that individual birds returned to the same feeder sites across three consecutive years.
- She also found that sites with more flowering shrubs nearby tended to have higher return rates, though the pattern varied considerably from site to site.
- Okafor cautions that this association may reflect other site features, such as elevation, rather than the shrubs themselves.
- In a separate study, botanist Lien Tran showed that hummingbirds visiting shrub flowers increased seed production in those shrubs.
problem.question: The student wants to present both of Okafor's findings while accurately reflecting how strongly each is supported. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Okafor established that individual hummingbirds returned to the same feeder sites for three years, and she showed that nearby flowering shrubs cause birds to return at higher rates.

Okafor's banding records suggest that individual hummingbirds may have returned to the same feeder sites over three years, and sites with more flowering shrubs nearby tended to see higher return rates.

Okafor confirmed that individual hummingbirds returned to the same feeder sites for three years; she also observed a tendency, possibly explained by factors like elevation, for sites with more nearby flowering shrubs to have higher return rates.

Okafor confirmed that individual hummingbirds returned to the same feeder sites for three years, and she also observed that hummingbird visits tended to increase seed production in nearby flowering shrubs.
problem.explanation: 정답 C: 귀환 사실은 밴딩 기록으로 '확인(confirmed)'되었으므로 확정적으로, 관목과 귀환율의 관계는 '경향'이며 고도 등 다른 요인일 수 있으므로 잠정적으로 서술했다. A: 상관관계를 '원인(cause)'으로 과장했다. B: 확인된 귀환 사실을 'suggest…may have'로 불필요하게 축소했다. D: 확실성 수준은 그럴듯하지만, 종자 생산 증가는 Tran의 별도 연구 내용으로 Okafor의 결과가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. The banding records confirmed that birds returned, so it's right to state that as fact. The shrub link was only a tendency that might come from other site features, like elevation, so it has to be stated cautiously. C does both. A is wrong because it overstates a correlation as a cause ("cause birds to return"). B is wrong because it weakens a confirmed finding into a guess ("suggest... may have returned"). D uses hedging that sounds right, but it credits Okafor with the seed-production finding, which actually comes from Tran's separate study.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 확정적(밴딩 기록으로 confirmed) 진술과 잠정적(tended to, varied, 고도 등 다른 요인 가능) 진술이 공존하고, C는 각각의 확실성 수준을 정확히 반영하며 Okafor의 두 결과를 하나의 문장으로 통합한다. A는 상관을 인과(cause)로 과잉 일반화, B는 확인된 사실을 suggest/may have로 과도 축소, D는 Tran의 별도 연구 결과를 Okafor에 오귀속하여 각 오답의 결함이 명확하다. 해설도 지정 정답과 오답 사유를 정확히 뒷받침한다. 학생은 단순 사실 선택을 넘어 확실성 구분·출처 귀속·상관/인과 방향 판별을 동시에 수행해야 하므로 hard 적합.
